subject: mathematics
question_text: Let a = 2i − j + k and b = 3i + 4j − k. If θ is the angle between a and b, then find sin θ.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find sin of the angle between two vectors.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a×b and the magnitudes
steps.margin_note: First mark. SINE comes from the CROSS product, where cosine came from the dot — that is the one thing to get right here.

recall.must_convey: That sin θ comes from the CROSS product, and that |a×b| = √155 with |a| = √6 and |b| = √26.
accept: sine uses the cross product so find a cross b, its magnitude is root one fifty five
take the cross product because sine goes with cross, dot is for cosine
the cross product magnitude is root one hundred fifty five and the two lengths are root six and root twenty six
sine ki cross product vaadali, magnitude root one fifty five
find a cross b and the two magnitudes

steps.why: A cross product has magnitude |a||b| sin θ, exactly as a dot product has |a||b| cos θ. Choosing the right product is choosing the right trig ratio.
common_mistakes: Using the dot product, which gives cos θ instead.
Sign slip on the j term.

steps.label: Apply the sine formula
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Divide by the product of the two magnitudes. √6 times √26 is √156, so the surds combine into one fraction under a single root.

recall.must_convey: That sin θ = |a×b|/(|a||b|), which combines to √(155/156).
accept: sine theta is the cross product magnitude over the two lengths, root one fifty five over root one fifty six
divide to get root of one fifty five over one fifty six
sin theta equals root one fifty five by root one fifty six
sin theta root 155 by root 156 vasthundi
combine the surds into one root

steps.why: Two square roots multiplied become the root of the product, so √6·√26 = √156 — which lets the whole answer sit under one root.
common_mistakes: Adding the magnitudes instead of multiplying.
Leaving the answer as a decimal.
